summary: A logical interface is a software construct inside the host operating system, available in all popular operating systems. Mobile nodes in a Proxy Mobile IPv6 domain need it for network-based mobility features such as handoffs between technologies, multihoming and flow mobility. This informational RFC explains its support on IP hosts.

eli5.summary: One virtual plug in a computer that hides several real connections, so the network can switch between them without apps noticing.

questions: logical interface in proxy mobile ipv6
how does logical interface support proxy mobile ipv6
what is multihoming in mobile networks
subtitle: How hosts hide multiple network connections behind a single virtual interface.

tldr.problem: Mobile devices with multiple network interfaces (WiFi, LTE, Ethernet) need to switch between them seamlessly without interrupting IP sessions, but applications and routing assume each connection has its own IP address.
tldr.mechanism: A logical interface is a software construct that groups multiple physical interfaces into one virtual interface, hiding technology changes from the IP layer while maintaining a single IP address across handoffs.
tldr.outcome: Enables mobile devices in Proxy Mobile IPv6 networks to perform seamless handoffs between technologies, support simultaneous connections, and move traffic between interfaces without breaking applications.

facts.label: Physical interface (PIF)
facts.value: A hardware network module (Ethernet, WiFi, LTE, etc.)

facts.label: Logical interface (LIF)
facts.value: A software virtual interface grouping multiple PIFs

facts.label: Sub-interface (SIF)
facts.value: A physical or logical interface that is part of a logical-interface construct

today: RFC 7847 is an Informational RFC published in May 2016. It has not been obsoleted and remains the primary specification for logical interface support in the context of Proxy Mobile IPv6. The mechanism is widely implemented in mobile operating systems including Android, iOS, Linux, Windows, and macOS for managing multi-interface scenarios in mobile devices.

sections.title: The Logical Interface Problem
sections.content:
A logical interface is a software construct inside the host operating system that groups multiple physical network interfaces (WiFi, LTE, Ethernet, etc.) behind a single virtual interface. This approach is crucial for Proxy Mobile IPv6 (PMIPv6) networks that need to support inter-technology handoffs, multihoming (simultaneous attachment to multiple networks), and flow mobility (moving individual traffic flows between interfaces).

The core insight is that when a mobile device switches from one physical interface to another—say from WiFi to LTE—applications and the network should not notice. A logical interface makes this invisible by:

  • Maintaining a single IP address visible to applications and the upper layers
  • Hiding the physical interfaces behind abstraction
  • Dynamically routing packets through whichever physical interface is active
  • Allowing sub-interfaces (physical interfaces) to be attached and detached dynamically

This is distinct from link-layer handoff within a single technology (like switching between WiFi access points), where mobility can be handled entirely at the link layer without IP involvement.
sections.eli5: A logical interface is like a universal adapter. The phone has multiple real connections (Ethernet, WiFi, LTE), but the IP layer only sees one virtual connection. When the phone switches real connections, the virtual one stays the same.

sections.title: Logical Interface Architecture
sections.content:
From the perspective of the IP stack and applications, a logical interface appears as an ordinary network interface with assigned IP addresses. The key difference is the internal structure:

A logical interface maintains a relationship to a set of sub-interfaces (physical interfaces like if_1 and if_2). The logical interface exposes transmit and receive services to the IP layer, but these are actually mapped to whichever physical sub-interface is currently active or suitable for a given flow.

Each logical interface maintains two key data structures:

  • LIF table: Lists all sub-interfaces and their status (UP, DOWN, policy constraints)
  • Flow table: Maps each active flow to the sub-interface currently carrying it

This structure allows the host to dynamically map traffic to interfaces. For locally-generated traffic, interface selection follows flow routing policies. When traffic for an existing flow arrives on a different sub-interface, the logical interface interprets this as a flow mobility trigger and updates its routing tables accordingly.
sections.eli5: The logical interface has two internal lists: one tracking which physical connections are available and working, and another tracking which conversations are using which physical connection. When a conversation switches physical connections, the list updates automatically.

sections.title: Mobility Management Use Cases
sections.content:
Three primary use cases drive logical interface requirements in PMIPv6 networks:

Multihoming: A mobile node is simultaneously attached to multiple access networks via different technologies. The logical interface presents these as a single interface to IP, while the network (via PMIPv6 signaling) binds the mobile node's prefix to multiple access gateways. The LMA maintains separate bindings for each access gateway, but from the mobile node's perspective, there is a single IP address accessible from all physical connections.

Inter-technology Handoff: A device moves from one access technology to another (WiFi to LTE). The physical interface changes, but the IP configuration and address remain the same. Applications experience no session interruption because the logical interface masks the technology change. PMIPv6 signaling between network elements ensures the local mobility anchor updates its forwarding to point to the new access gateway.

Flow Mobility: Individual flows are moved between different physical interfaces without affecting other flows. For example, a VoIP call stays on WiFi for low latency while a bulk download moves to LTE for better bandwidth. The logical interface's flow table tracks which flows use which interface, and PMIPv6 signaling can move subsets of a prefix between access gateways.
sections.eli5: Three scenarios show why this matters: plugging in multiple connections simultaneously without apps noticing, switching from one connection type to another without interrupting apps, and moving different apps to different connections while keeping all of them working.

sections.title: Configuration and Implementation
sections.content:
A logical interface can be configured statically or created dynamically by a connection manager application. The set of sub-interfaces may be fixed or dynamic, with interfaces added or removed as needed. Implementation details such as configuration methods are out of scope for this specification.

The IP layer is typically configured with a default router reachable via the logical interface. This default router can be internal to the logical interface—a logical router that determines which physical interface to use for each packet—or external.

All major operating systems provide some form of logical interface construct. The IETF Interfaces MIB (RFC 2863) and the YANG interface data model (RFC 7223) treat logical interfaces the same as physical interfaces, making logical interfaces a natural operating system construct rather than a special case.

The method by which routing policies are configured on the host is implementation-specific and out of scope. These policies guide interface selection for locally-generated traffic.
sections.eli5: The host operating system builds the logical interface, either from configuration set up ahead of time or dynamically as it connects to networks. The IP routing system can have policies to prefer one physical interface over another.

sections.title: Security and Operational Aspects
sections.content:
The logical interface implementation on the host is transparent to the network and does not expose the host to additional security vulnerabilities. However, there are security considerations worth noting:

Different physical access technologies have different security properties. A home WiFi network has user-controlled security, while an LTE network has operator-controlled security. Grouping interfaces with different security properties into one logical interface masks these differences from upper layers, which could have unintended consequences if security-aware applications expect to know which technology is in use.

The logical-interface approach works with PMIPv6 extensions (RFC 5213, RFC 5844) that were specifically designed to support these semantics. Modern operating systems including Linux, Windows, macOS, and Android have some form of logical interface support for managing multi-interface scenarios.

Flow-based routing policies on the host can be managed through various mechanisms, but standardization of policy expression is outside this specification's scope. The operational requirement is that the logical interface can apply consistent policies to direct traffic appropriately.
sections.eli5: The host's use of a logical interface doesn't create security problems by itself. But mixing connections with different security levels—like a trusted corporate WiFi and an untrusted coffee shop WiFi—can be risky, because the security properties are hidden from apps.

left.title: Without Logical Interface
left.desc: Multiple IP interfaces, each with different address. Apps must handle switching.

right.title: With Logical Interface
right.desc: One IP interface hides multiple physical connections. Apps see no change on switching.
